rationale: Iteration 1 scored 52.8 (best so far) but went off track on all 60 trials, each with one line-loss event and max_error of 0.061 to 0.065 m against the 0.06 m limit. The failure occurs at about 0.05 m offset, where the outer sensors (x = ±0.03) lose the tape. That matches the sensor-reach limit: with 16 mm footprints, the outer sensor sees tape only until the robot centre is about 0.05 m off the line. Iteration 0 showed that 12 mm footprints at x = ±0.04 were not enough on their own (score 26), so the footprint should stay at 16 mm. The Evaluator's requested revision is to widen the spread to x = +0.05, +0.025, 0, -0.025, -0.05, which should let the outer sensor see tape out to about 0.07 m, above the 0.06 m limit. This is the only geometry change against iteration 1. kp is 2.0 and kd is 0.15, which the Evaluator recommended. base_speed stays at 1.4 and line_loss stays at last_direction, so the sensor change is isolated. Expected result: line_loss_events drops to 0 or stays at 1 with a max_error that is now below 0.06 m, and progress rises above the iteration 1 level of about 0.12 to 0.16. Hypotheses to check: (1) if line_loss_events is 0 and max_error is below 0.06 m, raise base_speed toward 1.6 to reduce completion time; (2) if rms_error rises above about 0.04 m with the wider spread, the coarser signal is the cause, so reduce sensor_size to 0.012 while keeping the spread; (3) if one line-loss event remains with max_error above 0.06 m, the controller is limiting, so test kd at 0.1 and watch steering_oscillation (iteration 1 range 0.07 to 0.16).
